title: FairSplit: Decomposing the Embedding Space for Fair Classification
topic: Social Aspects->Fairness, Equity, Justice and Safety
claim: Standard embeddings entangle target and sensitive attributes, while decomposing them into separate spaces isolates sensitive information away from the prediction space.
layout: 2 side-by-side groups of 3 t-SNE scatter panels, shared legends below, rows colored by target then sensitive attribute
description: Two wide frames sit side by side, each holding three t-SNE scatter plots of CelebA embeddings. The left frame is colored by the target attribute (blue for not smiling, yellow for smiling). The right frame is colored by the sensitive attribute (light blue for female, maroon for male). Within each frame, the first panel is the Vanilla (ERM) embedding space. The other two are FairSplit's Fair Space and Sensitive Space. Bold headers sit above the panels, and the y-axes read 'Target Attribute' and 'Sensitive Attribute'. Legends sit at the bottom with colored dots. In the vanilla embedding, smiling and not smiling separate cleanly, and the female/male colors in the right frame overlap closely with that split. In the Fair Space, the target classes stay separated but female and male points are intermixed. In the Sensitive Space, gender separates clearly. The eye goes first to the colorful scatter clusters.
caption: Embedding spaces on CelebA-S, where the task is to predict whether a person is smiling and gender is the sensitive attribute, i.e., the protected characteristic on which predictions should not depend, visualized with t-SNE and colored by the target (left) and the sensitive attribute (right). Each side shows three panels: the Vanilla embedding, trained by empirical risk minimization (ERM) without fairness constraints, and the Fair Space and Sensitive Space of FAIRSPLIT. In the Vanilla (ERM) embedding, smiling/not smiling correlates with female/male. FAIRSPLIT instead classifies from the Fair Space, which is guided towards independence from the sensitive attribute.
abstract: Fair classification faces a twofold challenge: maintaining high classification accuracy while limiting reliance on sensitive information. Our method FairSplit achieves this by learning a decomposition of the embedding space into a Fair Space used for prediction and a Sensitive Space that isolates sensitive information. During training, the model must simultaneously learn the classification task and separate fair from sensitive information. The Sensitive Space gives sensitive attributes a destination, so the Fair Space can be used for prediction without relying on them. This decomposition is guided via a learnable mask and the Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion (HSIC) as a measure of statistical dependence. We provide theoretical guarantees showing that the demographic parity gap is upper-bounded by both (i) the learned dimensionality of the Fair Space and (ii) the HSIC between the Fair Space and sensitive attributes. FairSplit effectively handles multiclass tasks and non-binary sensitive attributes, overcoming key limitations of existing fair classification methods. Experiments on established fairness benchmarks show that FairSplit achieves competitive accuracy-fairness trade-offs. Code is available at https://github.com/shkabrii/fairsplit.
